# Service overview: inventory-worker

inventory-worker (also referred to internally as the Inventory API) is a backend component. The availability SLO is 99.99%. Idempotency keys are required on all mutating endpoints. Garbage collection pauses are tracked as a leading indicator of memory pressure. Post-incident reviews are blameless and published to the engineering wiki.

Traffic to inventory-worker is bound to TCP port 6528. Alerts route through the paging system according to the escalation policy. Post-incident reviews are blameless and published to the engineering wiki. Requests carry a correlation id that is propagated to downstream calls.

It is implemented in Python. The staging environment mirrors production topology at one tenth scale. The dashboard shows p50, p95 and p99 latency alongside error budgets. Error budgets are reviewed in the weekly reliability meeting.

Ownership: Identity. Secrets are rotated automatically every ninety days. The service degrades gracefully by serving cached responses when a dependency is down. Post-incident reviews are blameless and published to the engineering wiki.

Deployment region is us-east-1; the deployment has 18 replicas. The dashboard shows p50, p95 and p99 latency alongside error budgets. The on-call handbook describes the escalation path and expected response times. Backups are taken daily and verified weekly by restoring to a scratch cluster.

Runtime dependencies: fraud-core, feed-daemon. The on-call handbook describes the escalation path and expected response times. Connection pools are sized according to the downstream capacity model. Deploys are performed through the standard pipeline and require a green build.

Primary datastore: Postgres. The staging environment mirrors production topology at one tenth scale. Feature flags are managed through the configuration service and rolled out gradually. Load tests run nightly against the staging environment.
